**Current positioning (what the journal accepts now):** Analytic philosophy of religion and Christian philosophical theology: papers advancing or critiquing arguments for/against theism, historical-figure engagement (Kierkegaard, Newman, Malebranche), theodicy/problem-of-evil and divine-hiddenness work, and philosophy-and-science-of-religion crossover (e.g. origins-of-life research). Also runs regular book-review sections on new philosophy-of-religion/theology monographs.

**Methods noted as welcome (qualitative — not a scored 0-5 table, see Methodological Preferences below):** analytic argument-based philosophy of religion, historical philosophy (close readings of Kierkegaard, Newman, Malebranche, etc.), philosophical theology / doctrinal metaphysics (e.g. Trinity, hypostatic structure), science-and-religion / philosophy-of-science crossover (e.g. origins-of-life rationality), book reviews and critical discussion pieces
